blocks.t: Welcome to Orient's Hotpot Chronicles — a Minecraft mod about gathering around a bubbling hotpot. Build a stove, place a pot, pour in the broth, grind soybeans and press fresh tofu, harvest nine farmable seasonings and greens, simmer tripe and fatty beef rolls, grab bamboo chopsticks, mix your dipping sauce, and toast friends at the table.

Follow these six steps from scratch to eat your first hotpot meal. Every step includes a recipe.
Step 1: Make a stove
Place the stove on the ground and right-click its brick body with an empty hand to open the firebox screen.
Add fuel to the firebox slot — any vanilla furnace fuel works: planks, logs, sticks, charcoal, coal, lava buckets, and more. Stronger fuel cooks faster (see Stoves & Hotpots).
Step 2: Craft a pot and place it on the stove
Iron and copper pots behave identically apart from looks. Hold the pot and right-click the stove to mount it; its handles automatically face your left and right sides.
Tip
b: Want half spicy and half mild? Add a copper or iron ingot to make Yuanyang or four-grid divided pots — see Stoves & Hotpots.

blocks.t: Step 3: Pour in broth
Right-click the pot with a filled bucket or stew to add broth:
Right-click the pot with　Resulting broth
Clear Broth: balanced speed, cooks anything (add hotpot bases for Tomato / Three Delicacies broth)
Rich Stock: slowest (×0.85), milky white, filling and defensive
Mushroom Broth: brisk (×1.15), returns the empty bowl
Spicy Red Broth: fastest (×1.3), fiery red, boost spiciness with chili peppers
Once broth is poured in, steam rises. A pot without broth will not ignite the stove.
Step 4: Add raw ingredients
With broth inside, hold raw ingredients and right-click the pot. A pot has 3×3 (9) large cells; food enters whichever cell you aim at.

Keep it simple at first — vanilla raw beef, porkchop, mutton, and fish all work; mod items like Raw Tripe (from cows), Fatty Beef Roll (sliced with a knife), and Raw Chicken Feet (from adult chickens) feel extra authentic. See Ingredients & Cutting for processing and crops.
Note
b: Only put food in the pot. It accepts raw cookable foods only; already-cooked food cannot go back in.

blocks.t: Step 5: Craft bamboo chopsticks

Hold bamboo chopsticks and Shift + right-click the pot to open the Hotpot Screen: you can see every slot inside and tell raw from cooked food by sight; press G on a pot with cooked food (or click "Eat Challenge" top-right) for solo or multiplayer rush/rhythm minigames (disabled by default in Simple Mode).
Step 6: Eat!
Eat inside the screen: with chopsticks on your cursor, left-click cooked food to eat it in one bite (complete with crunch and burp).
Pick up without the screen: right-click the pot directly with bamboo chopsticks to pick up one cooked portion from the targeted cell, then hold right-click to eat it.
Scoop by hand or bowl: empty-handed (or holding a bowl) right-click picks up cooked food directly from that cell.
Skip cold pots: food never cooks in an unlit cold pot, and eating from one carries a 30% chance of 15 s Nausea (switch to Simple Mode or disable penalties in Mod Settings if preferred).
A lit pot also continuously heals nearby players within 6 blocks (Regeneration I) — gather friends around the stove!

◆ Short and tall stoves
Brick Stove: the short version. Its brick surface sits flush with a low hotpot table.

Tall Brick Stove: raises the firebox and pot by 10 pixels to match a tall hotpot table (its brick surface sits two pixels below the tabletop while the pot rim rises three pixels above for easy access).

A tall stove also occupies the block above it with an invisible block — leave that space empty when placing one. Once mounted with a pot, if a click misses the pot slot you can right-click the lower brick body to reliably open the firebox, and the upper hitbox updates immediately whenever a pot is placed or removed. Both short and tall stoves match adjacent vanilla bricks cleanly on all four sides whether lit or unlit, leaving only firebox flames and embers glowing warmly.
◆ Fuel and heat

Right-click the stove's brick body (or the stove itself when no pot is attached) to open the firebox screen and add fuel. Any vanilla furnace fuel works, with the same burn time as a furnace. There are three heat levels:
Fuel　Heat　Burn time (same as a furnace)
Wood items (planks, logs, sticks, etc.)　×0.65　For example, planks: 15 seconds
Coal or charcoal　×1.0　80 seconds
Lava bucket　×1.6　1000 seconds
Tip
b: Fuel is consumed only while raw ingredients need cooking. If the pot has broth and the firebox has fuel but there is no raw food, the fire stays lit and the broth keeps bubbling evenly without consuming fuel — take your time setting the table without wasting coal. An empty pot without broth will not light the stove.

blocks.t: The firebox screen has no temperature bar or countdown timer — watch the flame size to see how strongly it burns.
◆ Types
Pot　Description
Iron Nine-Grid Hotpot / Copper Nine-Grid Hotpot　Nine-grid pot: one broth across nine large cells. Copper and iron differ only in appearance.
Yuanyang and four-grid pots　Available since 0.1.3-alpha-hotfix1; see Yuanyang and four-grid pots below.
Choose copper or iron, then select a pot shape below:
A pot is an independent block: it can sit on a stove, on the ground, or on a lit campfire.
◆ Capacity
A nine-grid pot has 9 large cells, each containing a 3×3 grid of 9 smaller slots — up to 81 portions per pot. Food enters the large cell under your crosshair; once full, no more fits there.
◆ Broth bases
Add this　Broth　Cooking speed　Notes
Clear Broth　×1.00　Clear and light
Rich Stock　×0.85　Milky white; slowest
Mushroom Broth　×1.15　Returns the bowl when poured
Spicy Red Broth　×1.30　Bright red; fastest
Tomato Broth　×1.10　Craft a broth bucket from hotpot base + water bucket, or add base to Clear Broth
Three Delicacies Broth　×1.00　Same method with Three Delicacies Hotpot Base

Hotpot bases: Tomato Hotpot Base uses tomatoes and Three Delicacies Hotpot Base uses Three Delicacies ingredients (see Recipe Collection). Dropping a base into Clear Broth converts the pot directly, just like pouring a crafted broth bucket.
Add broth: hold a bucket (or mushroom stew) and right-click the pot. Standard pots hold one broth at a time (divided pots hold multiple).
Remove broth: right-click with an empty bucket to scoop broth back out. Mushroom broth requires a bowl and no food left in the pot — take out all food first.
Serve soup to drink: right-click with a bowl to collect cooked food first, or soup if none is cooked; see Tableware & Drinks.
◆ Four heat levels for Spicy Red Broth
Spicy Red Broth can be dialed up — not with powder, by throwing real chili peppers into the pot.
Level　Effect on food cooked in that pot
Mild (just poured)　Strength I for 6 s, Speed I for 6 s, no Hunger
Medium Spicy　Strength II for 9 s, Speed I for 9 s
Extra Spicy　Strength II for 12 s, Speed I for 10 s, Fire Resistance 15 s, and Hunger I 6 s (spice opens your appetite)
Level 3 Extreme Spicy　Strength II for 15 s, Speed I for 12 s, Fire Resistance 30 s, and Hunger I 8 s; your mouth bursts into harmless flame for 2 s (prevented by a cloth apron)
How to adjust it:

Hold a Chili Pepper chili pepper and right-click the red broth area: heat goes up one level with a burst of flame and an action-bar message. At Extreme Spicy it notifies you without consuming the pepper.
Cool down with ice: regular Ice drops 1 level, Packed Ice drops 2, and Blue Ice resets straight to Mild with white steam and splashes.
Clicking any other broth with chili or ice warns that only Spicy Red Broth can be adjusted and will not insert them as food.
Yuanyang and four-grid pots track each compartment separately — only the compartment you click changes. Pouring, scooping, swapping broths, or emptying resets heat back to Mild.
A bowl of Bowl of Spicy Red Broth scooped from the pot keeps the heat level at the moment it was scooped. Cooked food also shows its heat level, such as "Broth: Spicy Red Broth · Extra Spicy".
Simple Mode
b: Penalties are currently disabled: Extra Hot spicy food no longer inflicts Hunger or sets your mouth briefly on fire, while Strength, Speed, and Fire Resistance remain active.

blocks.t: Tip
b: Pair spice levels with chili oil, honey, and vinegar: chili oil grants Fire Resistance, while honey and vinegar clear the Hunger debuff and suppress the 2-second mouth flame. Spicy step durations, Fire Resistance, Hunger, and mouth-flame thresholds can also be tuned in Configurable values under "Spicy Broth" (Simple Mode or disabling mode.penalties_enabled skips the Hunger and mouth-flame penalties).

blocks.t: ◆ What the broth adds to your food
Food cooked in a pot carries that broth's signature flavor — tooltips gain a line such as "Broth: Mushroom Broth" (plus heat level for Spicy Red Broth) and grant an extra effect when eaten:
Broth　Extra effect from food cooked in it
Clear Broth　Speed I for 15 s (clean and light) + 1 tick of Saturation
Rich Stock　Resistance I for 15 s + Absorption I for 30 s (beef bones and old hen, hearty and protective)
Mushroom Broth　Regeneration I for 10 s (mountain mushrooms, restorative)
Spicy Red Broth　Strength + Speed scaled by that compartment's heat level; Extra Spicy+ adds Fire Resistance and Hunger (see above)
Tomato Broth　Haste I for 15 s (sweet and tangy energy boost), also clears Nausea
Three Delicacies Broth　Water Breathing for 20 s + Luck I for 30 s (scallops and shrimp, fortune smiles)
It counts whether you pick food up by hand, eat with chopsticks, or ladle into a bowl. Simmer a batch in Mushroom Broth to heal up, or brew Three Delicacies Broth before diving.

Hovering over a dish or soup bowl indents and lists every status effect and duration right below the broth line (e.g., "Strength II (0:15)", "Speed I (0:12)") — blue for buffs, red for debuffs. Dipping in honey or vinegar suppresses Hunger so it disappears from the tooltip too. Soup bowls list their effects the exact same way.
◆ How food cooks
Raw ingredients turn into cooked dishes using their smoker / campfire recipes or pot-only boiling recipes (anything a smoker cooks can simmer in the pot):

b: Time per portion = base cooking time ÷ (fuel heat × broth multiplier)

blocks.t: For example, raw beef takes 5 seconds in a smoker, so Coal + Clear Broth takes 5 seconds; Spicy Red Broth (×1.3) takes ~3.8 seconds, while wood (×0.65) takes ~7.7 seconds. Small cuts like fatty beef rolls, potato slices, meatballs, and boneless chicken feet take half as long as whole meat.
See the "Cooking" and "Pot-Only Boiling" sections of the Recipe Collection for exact times.
Note
b: Only put food in the pot: only raw cookable foods can be inserted; already-cooked food, chili peppers, milled spices, and items tagged orients_hotpot_chronicles:not_pot_ingredient are rejected.

blocks.t: ◆ Ways to add and remove things
What you are holding　Right-clicking the pot does this
Raw ingredient　Adds it to the large cell under your crosshair
A plate of food　Tips raw ingredients into available large cells; cooked food stays on the plate
Bamboo chopsticks holding raw food　Drops that ingredient into the targeted cell
Bamboo chopsticks holding cooked food　Eats it (even when full; sneak + right-click a plate/bowl to put back)
Bamboo chopsticks (empty)　Picks up a cooked portion from that cell (notifies if none); hold right-click to eat
Bamboo chopsticks + sneak (Shift)　Opens the hotpot screen
Bucket　Pours broth in, or scoops broth out with an empty bucket
Bowl　Collects cooked food first, or serves soup
Empty hand　Collects cooked food from the targeted cell
Empty hand + sneak (Shift)　Packs the pot (with broth and food intact) into your inventory
Tip
b: Chopsticks and empty hands pick up whichever portion is currently visible at the surface; if it is still raw, a message warns you. A bowl collects the visible cooked portion plus other cooked food, up to 3 portions total.

blocks.t: ◆ Hoppers and pots
A hopper above the pot inserts only raw cookable ingredients, one per slot; everything else remains in the hopper.
A hopper below the pot (or stove) extracts only cooked dishes, leaving raw food to finish cooking.
Hold bamboo chopsticks and Shift + right-click the pot to open it (plain right-click picks up food instead):

Every portion is rendered individually (raw vs cooked appearances), and bubbles, steam, and floating ingredients maintain a steady, smooth phase throughout burning with smooth ignition/extinguish transitions.
With chopsticks on your cursor, left-click cooked food to eat it in one bite (restores hunger and saturation, works even when full).
Double-click to gather matching cooked portions onto your cursor like a vanilla inventory.
Hover over ingredients for names and "Dipped: ..." tooltips.
Holding dipping sauce in your main or off hand automatically dips each bite eaten in this screen.
◆ Cold pots

A pot is cold when it is not on a lit stove or lit campfire. Broth sits still and food floats uncooked. Eating from a cold pot has a 30% chance of causing Nausea for 15 seconds (adjust chance/duration under "Cold-Pot Nausea" in Configurable values, or skip completely in Simple Mode / with mode.penalties_enabled off). Drink a Plant Protein Drink, Clear Broth bowl, or dip in vinegar to clear Nausea.
Simple Mode
b: Penalties are currently disabled: eating from an unheated pot will not inflict Nausea, though unheated pots still cannot cook raw food.

blocks.t: Skip building a stove by placing the pot on a lit campfire or soul campfire:
Slender iron supports extend automatically under the pot to rest on the campfire logs cleanly without floating or flame clipping.
Heat equals coal with zero fuel cost, and still heals nearby players; the screen indicates active heating.
Extinguishing or breaking the campfire turns the pot cold; empty-hand Shift + right-click packs the whole pot cleanly just like on a stove.

A heated pot refreshes Regeneration I for 10 seconds every 4 seconds on players within 6 blocks. Staying by the table keeps hearts topped up. (Adjust interval, radius, duration, and level under "Pot Warmth" in Configurable values; set duration to 0 to disable.)

entries.title: Real-time minigames: Speed Eating and 4-Track Rhythm Battle

blocks.t: Aim at a pot containing cooked food and press [G] (or click "Eat Challenge" top-right inside the hotpot screen) to launch a solo high-score run or send a 15-second duel invite to tablemates within 8 blocks ([G] accepts / [N] declines popups; /orientshotpot minigame can also start solo runs, invite, accept/decline, or list tracks).

Food source: by default, consumes real cooked food from the pot and triggers dipping sauces, broth buffs, hunger/saturation, and the "Gather Around the Stove" / "Table Feast" advancements; toggle "Virtual Practice Platter" on the challenge panel to practice without consuming food (hosts can disable this option).

Mode 1 · Speed Eating (Rush): a 10-second frenzy hammering Spacebar; every 5 valid hits eats 1 cooked portion with a burst of steam. Emptying the pot awards a "Clean Plate" bonus and ends early; the server enforces a sliding-window limit via minigame.rush_max_cps (default 16 CPS) to block macros.

Mode 2 · 4-Track Rhythm Battle: a translucent 4-track falling-note overlay using D / F / J / K by default (arrow keys also work; fully rebindable in vanilla Key Binds), judged by rhythm_perfect_ms (60ms) / rhythm_good_ms (130ms) / rhythm_miss_ms (220ms). Includes 3 built-in tracks (midnight_boil, bamboo_chopsticks, red_soup_rush) and supports custom datapack charts under data//hotpot_tracks/*.json (/reload applies immediately and syncs to multiplayer clients).
Simple Mode
b: Instant Minigames are disabled in the current mode. Re-enable them in Settings -> Mode & Options or run /orientshotpot mode full to play Rush or 4-Lane Rhythm.

blocks.t: Combine a matching copper or iron ingot with a nine-grid pot of the same metal to craft a divided pot: ingot on the left = Taiji Yuanyang; below = Round-Center Yuanyang; above = Straight-Divider Yuanyang; one on each side = Four-Grid Pot; one above and one below = Square-Center Yuanyang. Each compartment holds its own broth, fills/scoops independently where you aim, and cooks using its own broth (empty compartments do not cook). They sit on the ground, campfires, short stoves, and tall stoves alike.
Pot　Divider　Broths　Capacity per compartment
Taiji Yuanyang　S-shaped yin-yang curve　2　28 each side
Round-Center Yuanyang　Circular center ring　2　44 outer, 9 center
Straight-Divider Yuanyang　Straight center partition　2　36 each side
Four-Grid Pot　Cross partition (4 zones)　4　16 per zone
Square-Center Yuanyang　Circular ring with square center　2　44 outer, 9 center
Note
b: In 0.1.4-alpha, S-shaped and O-shaped pots were renamed Taiji Yuanyang and Round-Center Yuanyang along with their item IDs. Those four renamed pots already placed in 0.1.3 or earlier worlds will disappear (two each in copper and iron).

blocks.t: Open the screen with bamboo chopsticks (Shift + right-click). Small slots fill outward from the pot walls; gaps near dividers too small for full slots remain open showing simmering broth and pot bottom. Each compartment floats ingredients across dedicated spots (Taiji: 4 per side; Round/Square-Center: 6 outer + 2 inner; Straight: 3 per side; Four-Grid: 2 per zone), cycling turns to float to the surface.
Inside the screen, double-clicking matching dishes or ladling with a bowl collects across compartments sharing the same broth — if broths differ, only the side you clicked is collected.
Iron divided pots use identical patterns with iron ingots and an iron nine-grid pot.

Mine the pot: only the pot breaks, packing broth and contents into one item restored upon placement; break debris, dropped pot, and spilled items spawn at the pot's true height rather than the stove base, and mining the upper section of a tall stove emits matching pot or brick particles. Middle-clicking in Creative also copies the packed pot intact.
Standalone pots stay suspended even over air without popping off.
Mine the stove bricks: mines the whole stove and drops the packed pot too.
Pot tooltips display stored broth and portion counts (how many are cooked).
To lift a pot off a stove without breaking bricks: Shift + right-click the pot with an empty hand.

Combine 2 raw meatballs + 1 Cilantro shapelessly for 2 cilantro meatballs (available for all four meat/fish balls). Cooked ones restore 4 hunger each.
Shrimp: caught by fishing (~1/6 weight).
Peeled shrimp: slice shrimp on a cutting board or stonecutter.
Shrimp paste: pound peeled shrimp 3 times with a rolling pin.
All three restore 1 raw, or 3 / 3 / 4 cooked (cooked shrimp & peeled shrimp carry fun tooltip lines).
Cut raw porkchop once on a cutting board or stonecutter for 1 minced pork (pounding porkchop still makes pork meatballs).
Shapelessly craft minced pork + 1 wheat for 3 raw ham sausages.
Cook in a pot, furnace, smoker, or campfire to obtain ham sausage.
Slice ham sausage once on a cutting board or stonecutter for 3 ham sausage slices (raw sausages cannot be sliced).
Cook ham sausage slices once more into cooked ham sausage slices (cannot go back into the pot afterwards).
Tip
b: Chain order: Raw Porkchop → Minced Pork → Raw Ham Sausage → Ham Sausage → Ham Sausage Slice → Cooked Ham Sausage Slice. Minced pork is an intermediate ingredient and cannot be eaten directly.

blocks.t: Soybeans: grow directly on farmland or harvest wild soybean clusters, with a fallback grass drop (2% default; restores 15% in Simple Mode).
Full Mode (default) 3-step traditional tofu workflow:

Wet-grind soymilk on a Stone Mill: crafted with vanilla cobblestone and uniform upper/lower shading under shaders, standing ~1.5 blocks tall so its front spout aligns with the rim of an adjacent open vat. Load 2 soybeans and pour a water bucket (1 bucket yields 3 wet grinds by default), then empty-hand right-click 4 full turns to grind soymilk — if the spout faces an empty Open Wooden Vat, finished soymilk automatically pours over the rim into the vat (standalone mills collect soymilk into the annular trough for scooping into Soymilk Bucket, which can also be drunk for 2 hunger); you can also dry-grind crushed peanuts (3 turns → 2), garlic paste (3 turns → 2), and chopped millet chili (2 turns → 2).

Coagulate & press in an Open Wooden Vat: once the vat holds soymilk, add Brine Bottle (kelp or dried kelp + water bucket + glass bottle) and cover with a 3D Wooden Press Lid; lid and liquid surface smoothly lower together over 4 seconds to press 2 cold tofu (empty hand retrieves lid and tofu; emptying the vat immediately triggers waiting soymilk from an adjacent mill to pour across).

Mode compatibility: switching to Simple Mode or turning off "Detailed Tofu Processing" (mode.detailed_tofu_processing) re-enables direct crafting-grid cold tofu from 2–3 soybeans + water bucket while keeping the mill and vat usable.
Simple Tofu Crafting
b: Detailed Tofu Processing is disabled: craft Cold Tofu directly on a crafting grid with 2 or 3 Soybeans + a Water Bucket. The Stone Mill and Open Wooden Vat still work normally.

blocks.t: Slice cold tofu once on a cutting board for 3 cold tofu cubes (cook for 2 hunger each), or cut cold tofu in a stonecutter into 2 dried tofu.
Tip
b: Cold tofu vs hot tofu:
Tofu (Cold)、Tofu (Hot)、Tofu Cube (Hot)
• Simmering whole cold tofu for 10 seconds cooks it into hot tofu (already cooked — scoop with hand/chopsticks; cannot go back in).
• Leaving hot tofu simmering for 30 seconds total breaks it into hot tofu cubes with equal count — fish out whole tofu early if you want whole blocks!
• Hot tofu also cuts into 3 hot tofu cubes; cold tofu cubes cook into hot cubes too.
• Server admins can adjust cooking.tofu_cook_ticks (default 200 ticks = 10 s) and cooking.tofu_overcook_ticks (default 600 ticks = 30 s) followed by /orientshotpot reload.

blocks.t: Crisp golden bites that always disappear off the table first:
Combine minced pork + wheat + 1 egg shapelessly for 3 raw crispy pork (1 hunger; seasoned raw batter — best cooked first).
Cook in a furnace (10 s) / smoker (5 s) / campfire (30 s) or hotpot for crispy pork (4 hunger — crunchy straight off the tray).
Simmer crispy pork one more time in the pot (~7.5 seconds on Coal + Clear Broth) for boiled crispy pork (6 hunger — juicy inside, tender outside).
Boiled crispy pork is the final stage and cannot be simmered again.
Tip
b: Order: Raw Porkchop → Minced Pork → Raw Crispy Pork → Crispy Pork → Boiled Crispy Pork. Fry half to snack crisp and simmer the rest in broth!

blocks.t: Arrange cold tofu or potato slices horizontally or vertically to craft four broth-soaking favorites:
Make　Pattern　Output　Raw hunger　Cooked hunger
2 × Cold Tofu side-by-side (horizontal)　3　2　4
2 × Cold Tofu stacked (vertical)　3　2　4
2 × Potato Slices side-by-side (horizontal)　3　1　4
2 × Potato Slices stacked (vertical)　3　1　4
Dried tofu stays chewy and nutty; tofu skin softens in seconds and traps broth inside its folds.
Wide noodles are famously slippery with chopsticks; sweet potato skin brings gentle starch sweetness.
All four cook in ~5–7.5 seconds (tofu skin & sweet potato skin 5 s; dried tofu & wide noodles 7.5 s), or via furnace / smoker / campfire.
Tip
b: Orientation decides the product: horizontal cold tofu = dried tofu, vertical = tofu skin; horizontal potato slices = wide noodles, vertical = sweet potato skin.

blocks.t: Enoki mushroom: craft from 2 brown mushrooms, or get 50% drops from breaking small brown/red mushrooms. Cooks in 2.5 seconds (3 hunger cooked) — long bundles built to soak up broth.
Greens: farm on farmland or gather wild greens (2% sparse grass fallback; 15% in Simple Mode). Cooks whole in 2.5 seconds (3 hunger) for the freshest bite at a spicy table.

Lotus root: 50% drop from breaking lily pads (shears drop lily pads instead). Slice whole roots on a cutting board (3 cuts, 1 slice each) or stonecutter (3 slices at once). Slices cook in 5 seconds (3 hunger) with crisp holes full of broth.
Raw squid: dropped by squids and glow squids (1–2, +0–1 per Looting). Whole squid must be scored once into 3 squid rolls before cooking (5 seconds, 4 hunger cooked), curling up neatly in hot broth.
All cook identically in furnaces (10 s), smokers (5 s), and campfires (30 s).
Tip
b: Enoki and greens tie with beef loin slices and tripe for fastest cooking; lotus slices and squid rolls take medium time; whole lotus root and whole squid prompt you to slice them first.

blocks.t: Shapelessly craft 1 wheat + 1 egg + 1 scallion + 1 bowl for 1 Egg Fried Rice.
Restores 7 hunger — fluffy gold-and-white grains flecked with fresh green scallion, ideal for soothing spice.
Egg fried rice is ready to eat and does not go in the pot; the bowl is part of the meal.
Source: grow on farmland or harvest wild chili peppers in plains/jungles, or break grass (2% sparse fallback; 15% in Simple Mode).
Eat raw for 1 hunger, or cut once on a cutting board / stonecutter / dry-grind 2 turns on the Stone Mill to get 2 Chopped Millet Chili.
Chopped Millet Chili is the 14th seasoning at the Sauce Station, granting Strength I for 8 s.
Most importantly, turn up Spicy Red Broth heat: hold a chili pepper and right-click the red broth area up to Level 3 Extreme Spicy; cool down with ice (see Stoves & Hotpots).
Note
b: Chili peppers and millet chili never go into the pot: right-clicking a pot with them only adjusts red broth heat or prompts you.

blocks.t: Source: grow on farmland or gather wild houttuynia in lush forests / riverbanks, or break grass (2% sparse fallback; 15% in Simple Mode).
Crunchy white root edible raw (1 hunger) with an unmistakable botanical punch.
Slice once on a cutting board or stonecutter into 3 houttuynia slices (whole roots must be sliced before entering the pot).
Houttuynia slices simmer 10 seconds (200 ticks) into cooked houttuynia slices (3 hunger), or roast normally.
Pound a whole root 3 times with a rolling pin on the cutting board for 2 minced houttuynia.
Minced Houttuynia is the 15th seasoning at the Sauce Station: grants Resistance I for 10 s and cures Poison.
Tip
b: Mellowed by simmering: raw houttuynia is bold, whereas cooking for 10 seconds leaves a mild sweet finish.

blocks.t: Source: killing adult chickens has a 50% base chance to drop 1–2 Raw Chicken Feet (+10% per Looting level; fire kills drop cooked chicken feet; configurable).
Deboning: slice raw chicken feet once on a cutting board or stonecutter to yield 1 Boneless Chicken Feet.
Cooked chicken feet (7.5 s pot / furnace) restore 3 hunger; cooked boneless chicken feet (faster 5 s cook) restore 4 hunger — tender collagen made for dry dipping spices.

Standalone orange trees: naturally spawn in Forests, Flower Forests, Plains, Meadows, and Jungles — vanilla oak and dark oak leaves no longer drop oranges. Right-click Orange Logs / Wood with an axe to strip them (burn into charcoal or craft 4 oak planks). Trees grow into compact orchard canopies with 1 exposed trunk block beneath a 3×3×2 main crown (optional 1 top leaf block) reachable from the ground; Orange Leaves mature through green → flowering → unripe citrus → ripe fruit (bonemeal works), yielding 1–2 Orange on right-click. Azalea-style transparent leaf textures obey vanilla Fast / Fancy graphics, allow players and mobs to pass gently through leaves (~1/5 cobweb drag), drop Orange Saplings when broken (recoverable intact via shears / Silk Touch), and wave gently under shaders alongside saplings.

9 plantable farmland crops: Scallion, Cilantro, Soybean, Garlic, Tomato, Chili Pepper, Peanut, Bok Choy, and Houttuynia Root require no separate seeds — recolored into vanilla moss/olive-green palettes with clear stage 2 → stage 3 mature silhouettes (umbels, exposed peanut pods, garlic bulbs, leafy bok choy heads), simply right-click farmland with the crop itself (bonemeal supported; drops 2–4 upon maturity; growth rate & bonemeal toggled in Config under "Crops & Fruit Trees").

Wild plants & grass fallback: wild clusters spawn naturally across plains/forest/savanna/jungle/riverbank biomes with vanilla small-flower tags for grass blending and shader waving, dropping 1–2 starter crops (shears / Silk Touch collect the decorative bush). With "Crops Replace Grass Drops" active (default on), breaking grass acts only as a sparse fallback (2% each); disabling it or switching to Simple Mode restores legacy grass drop rates (15%–25%). Enoki (mushrooms) and lotus root (lily pads) keep their original gathering methods.
Simple Mode
b: Crops Replace Grass Drops is disabled: breaking short/tall grass uses the classic higher drop rates (15%-25%), while farming and wild crops still work.

blocks.t: Source: scallions, cilantro, garlic, tomatoes, and soybeans now grow via farmland farming & wild clusters, keeping a 2% grass fallback (25% / 15% restored in Simple Mode).
Both are edible raw (1 hunger), used as Sauce Station seasonings, and cilantro crafts cilantro meatballs.
Grass, lily pad, mushroom, cow, and chicken drop chances can all be configured in Configurable values under "Loot Drop Chances" (including the standalone tomato key; run /reload after editing).
Cooked kelp: boil vanilla kelp in the hotpot for cooked kelp (furnaces/smokers/campfires still make dried kelp), restoring 2 hunger.

b: Unsure how long something cooks? Remember four tiers: beef loin slices, tripe, enoki, greens finish fastest; rolls, potato slices, tofu cubes, sausage slices, peeled shrimp, lotus slices, squid rolls, tofu skin, sweet potato skin, boneless chicken feet cook quickly; dried tofu, wide noodles, meatballs, crispy pork, chicken feet are medium; and whole beef loin and houttuynia slices take longest. Exact seconds are in Recipe Collection under "Cooking" and "Pot-Only Boiling".

blocks.t: A great dipping sauce completes hotpot. Use the self-service sauce station: 9 porcelain bowls let you mix any combination — every seasoning's buff stacks together.
In this chapter
Click an entry below to jump to it; you can also use the bookmarks along the top, or the triangle at the bottom right to turn page by page.
Sauce stations　Appearance: three ascending steppe…
15 seasonings　Garlic, peanuts, chili peppers, an…
Placing sesame paste & oyster sauce　Beyond seasoning bowls, sesame pas…
Mixing a sauce　Hold an empty bowl (Bowl) and righ…
Dipping food　Three easy ways to dip:
Appearance: three ascending stepped tiers holding 3 porcelain bowls each (9 total).
Height: 1.5 blocks tall, occupying 2 blocks cleanly (step right up onto each tier).
Materials: 11 wood styles plus iron (12 variants total).
Facing: faces the player who placed it.
◆ Recipes
Crafts 1 station per recipe. Swap planks with iron ingots for iron, or use matching wood planks.
◆ Restocking the bowls
Right-click the sauce station with an empty hand to open its restocking screen:
9 slots map to the 9 bowls on the station (15 seasonings exist in total; stock up to 9 kinds at once).
Each slot holds one ingredient type (multiple slots can repeat the same seasoning).
1 ingredient = 4 servings of seasoning, up to 16 ingredients (64 servings) per slot.
Click top-right ? for the ingredient reference sheet.
Stocked bowls show matching spices directly in the station model.
Tip
b: The ingredient reference uses a single paginated column. Clicking ? opens a narrow panel matching the main GUI width with wrapped names and effects; page via bottom arrows or mouse wheel, and reopening remembers your last page. JEI and REI automatically keep clear of the combined panel area.

blocks.t: Seasoning　Ingredient　Effect when eaten
MSG　Wheat　Restores 2 extra hunger
Chili Oil　Blaze Powder　Fire Resistance for 10 s
Sweet and Sour Sauce　Sweet Berries　Speed for 10 s
Honey　Honey Bottle　Clears spice Hunger and Poison
Sesame Oil　Sunflower or Pumpkin Seeds　Regeneration for 5 s
Vinegar　Apple or Beetroot　Clears Nausea and spice Hunger
Sugar　Sugar　Haste for 10 s
Chopped Scallion　Scallion　Flavor only, no effect
Minced Cilantro　Cilantro　Flavor only, no effect
Garlic Paste　Garlic Paste　Resistance for 8 s
Oyster Sauce　Oyster Sauce　Water Breathing for 10 s
Sesame Paste　Sesame Paste　Absorption I for 10 s
Crushed Peanuts　Crushed Peanuts　Jump Boost I for 10 s
Chopped Millet Chili　Chopped Millet Chili　Strength I for 8 s
Minced Houttuynia　Minced Houttuynia　Resistance I for 10 s, cures Poison

Garlic, peanuts, chili peppers, and houttuynia can be grown directly on farmland or gathered from wild plants (grass retains a 2% fallback under Crops Replace Grass, or 15% in Simple Mode). Make garlic paste by pounding garlic 3 times with a rolling pin or dry-grinding 3 turns on the Stone Mill for 2 portions; the last five are prepared as follows:
Oyster Sauce: shapelessly craft vanilla kelp + sugar + glass bottle for 2 bottles — great for underwater foraging.
Sesame Paste: peanut + wheat seeds + bowl crafts 2 bowls of rich soothing paste.
Crushed Peanuts: pound a peanut 3 times on a cutting board with a rolling pin or dry-grind 3 turns on the Stone Mill for 2 portions.
Chopped Millet Chili: slice a chili pepper once on a cutting board / stonecutter or dry-grind 2 turns on the Stone Mill for 2 portions (see Ingredients & Cutting).
Minced Houttuynia: pound a whole houttuynia root 3 times on a cutting board for 2 portions of detoxifying spice (see Ingredients & Cutting).
“Cools spice” removes Hunger triggered by Spicy Red Broth. Dipped food carries every seasoning's effect from that bowl simultaneously.
Beyond seasoning bowls, sesame paste jars and oyster sauce bottles can sit on tables as decor:

Place: hold either bottle and Shift + right-click an empty spot on a low/tall hotpot table — shares plate slots with bowls and chopsticks (sesame paste is a short white-labeled jar; oyster sauce is a tall dark bottle).
Pick up: empty-hand right-click returns the bottle; mining takes only that bottle. Breaking the table drops all tableware in that cell.
Purely decorative: table bottles cannot season or dip food directly — mix sauces at the sauce station or dip at a placed sauce bowl.
Bottles remain edible directly as food too.
Tip
b: Mix bottles, sauce bowls, chopsticks, and plates in one grid space to build an authentic hotpot tabletop!

blocks.t: Hold an empty bowl (Bowl) and right-click a stocked seasoning bowl on the station to create Dipping Sauce.
Hold that dipping sauce and right-click other stocked bowls to layer more seasonings.
Rules:
Each seasoning adds once per bowl.
One bowl holds 9 dips.
Mid-use bowls can still accept new unadded seasonings without changing remaining dips.
Clicking an empty station slot prompts you to restock.
Tooltips list every added seasoning and remaining dips.
Tip
b: Classic combo: Sesame Oil + Vinegar + Chopped Scallion + Minced Cilantro for healing, clearing spice/Nausea, and aroma; pair Spicy Red Broth with Honey or Vinegar.

blocks.t: Three easy ways to dip:
◆ ① Dip at the table
Set your dipping sauce on a table (right-click tabletop like a plate).
Right-click that sauce bowl while holding food with chopsticks (empty chopsticks warn you first).
Dipped food displays “Dipped: …”; the final dip leaves an empty bowl.
◆ ② Auto-dip while holding sauce
Hold dipping sauce in your main or off hand: eating food via chopsticks in the hotpot screen — or eating chopstick-held food in midair — automatically dips each bite.
◆ ③ Eat dipped food directly
Hold dipped food on chopsticks and hold right-click in midair to eat — effects apply regardless of how you consume dipped bites.
Each dip spends 1 charge out of 9 before returning an empty bowl.
Fill your hotpot table with plates of raw ingredients, bowls of soup, drinks to cool the spice, protective aprons, and chopsticks for picking up food.
In this chapter
Click an entry below to jump to it; you can also use the bookmarks along the top, or the triangle at the bottom right to turn page by page.
Plates　5 materials × 6 sizes = 30 plates:
Bowls and soup bowls　Vanilla bowls (Bowl) can sit on ta…
Drinks　One bottle gives 4 sips even when …
Cloth apron　Protect yourself from hot oil spla…
Chopsticks　Open hotpot screen: hold chopstick…
◆ Types
5 materials × 6 sizes = 30 plates:
Material　Small dish ingredient
Quartz　Nether Quartz
Woven bamboo　Bamboo
Terracotta　Brick
Copper　Copper Ingot
Iron　Iron Ingot
Size　Shape　Food capacity
Small dish (1×1)　One slot　3 portions
Two-slot plate (1×2)　Two slots long　6 portions
Three-slot long plate (1×3)　Three slots long　9 portions
Four-slot square plate (2×2)　Square　12 portions
Five-slot long plate (1×5)　Five slots long　15 portions
Eight-slot platter (2×4)　Large　24 portions
Each slot holds up to 3 portions of any food, so capacity = slots × 3.
◆ Crafting
Start with small dishes: arrange “material + bowl + material” horizontally to craft 2 small dishes, then combine matching small dishes into larger plates (quartz shown below):
◆ Placement
Hold a plate and right-click a tabletop or the ground to place it.
Multiple plates share one block without overlapping: up to 5 small dishes, 2 long plates, or 1 square plate per block (mixed as space permits).

Plates hug the tabletop automatically (5 px lower on low tables, 7 px higher on tall tables), and items placed on every plate size — including five-slot long plates, eight-slot platters, and small dishes — render cleanly layered without z-fighting or sinking under shaders.
◆ Adding and removing food
Actions apply to only the plate under your crosshair:
What you are holding　Right-clicking the plate does this
Plate　Places another plate
Food　Adds 1 portion (up to 3 per slot)
Bamboo chopsticks　Picks up the last-added portion; clicking while already holding cooked food = eats it (sneak + right-click to put back)
Empty hand　Picks up the whole plate with food
Empty hand + sneak　Pops the last-added portion into your inventory, leaving the plate
Mine a plate: breaks only the targeted plate and drops its food.
Middle-click: copies the plate including its contents.
Filled plates render their contents in inventory icons and in-hand, with bundle-style "×quantity" tooltips.
Tip into the pot: right-click the pot with a filled plate to pour raw ingredients in while cooked food stays on the plate.
◆ Vanilla bowls work too
Vanilla bowls (Bowl) can sit on tables too:
Place on a table like a plate: holds 3 portions cleanly layered without flicker.
Right-click a pot with a bowl: collects cooked food first (up to 3 portions), or ladles soup if none is cooked (without draining pot broth).
Right-click a pot with a food-filled bowl to tip everything inside.
◆ Six soup bowls
Ladled soup becomes a dedicated soup bowl item restoring 4 hunger plus its broth effect (custom broths without a dedicated bowl item fill the generic Soup Bowl):
Soup bowl　Effect
Speed I for 15 s + Saturation 1 tick; clears Nausea (clean and light)
Resistance I for 15 s + Absorption I for 30 s (high saturation, beef bones and old hen)
Regeneration I for 10 s (mountain mushrooms, restorative)

Strength + Speed (Mild: Strength I 6 s + Speed I 6 s; Medium Spicy: Strength II 9 s + Speed I 9 s; Extra Spicy: Strength II 12 s + Speed I 10 s + Fire Resistance 15 s + Hunger I 6 s; Level 3 Extreme Spicy: Strength II 15 s + Speed I 12 s + Fire Resistance 30 s + Hunger I 8 s). Keeps the pot's heat level when ladled; see heat levels
Haste I for 15 s; clears Nausea (sweet and tart)
Water Breathing for 20 s + Luck I for 30 s (scallops and shrimp)
Finished soup bowls return empty vanilla bowls and can also sit on tables.
Tip
b: Always use an empty bucket to change broth in the pot — ladling bowls is solely for drinking.

blocks.t: Drink　Effect per sip
Restores 2 hunger; Speed 15 s; cools spice (clears Hunger)
Restores 2 hunger; cools spice and clears Nausea
Restores 2 hunger; Speed and Haste 15 s; fizzes with bubbles
One bottle gives 4 sips even when full, leaving an empty bottle placeable on tables.
Place drinks on tables and right-click to sip; tooltips show remaining sips.
Craft Orange Drink from oranges, Plant Protein Drink from soybeans, and Orient Cola from cocoa beans and honey.
Starting in 0.3.1-alpha, pick ripe oranges directly off standalone orange trees in forests and plains (vanilla oak and dark oak leaves no longer drop oranges).
◆ Glass cups
Right-click an empty cup with a drink bottle to pour (Cup of Orange DrinkCup of Plant Protein DrinkCup of Orient Cola); 1 cup = 1 sip and returns the empty cup.
Finished bottles leave empty bottles (Empty Orange Drink BottleEmpty Plant Protein Drink Bottle) for decoration or refilling from cauldrons.

Cup of Water / Cup of Milk (Cup of WaterCup of Milk): right-click an empty cup with a water or milk bucket (bucket stays full), or scoop water sources directly; neither restores hunger, and milk clears effects.
◆ Toasting
Hold any filled glass cup (orange drink, plant protein drink, Orient Cola, water, or milk) and toast in three ways:
Right-click a friend also holding a filled cup in main or off hand to clink together.
Solo or casual toast: hold Shift and right-click air (prioritizes any cup-holding player within 4 blocks).
Right-click a filled cup placed on a table: clinks on the tabletop too.

A crisp double chime plays alongside rim splashes and cheerful music notes. Both players receive Luck I for 30 s + Regeneration I for 5 s, and the cup records +1 bonus hunger on its next sip (tooltip reads "Toasted · Restores +1 bonus Hunger when drunk").
Drinking resets the cup cleanly; toasting unlocks the "Cheers!" advancement. (Cooldown, buff durations/levels, and bonus hunger/saturation are tunable under "Cheers" in Configurable values.)
Tip
b: Start hotpot nights with a toast — boosted Luck helps you snag meatballs, and Shift + right-click air works solo anytime!

blocks.t: ◆ Drinks in cauldrons
Right-click a vanilla cauldron with a drink bottle or filled cup to pour it in (one drink type per cauldron, up to 12 sips / 3 bottles; level rises every 4 sips; cola bubbles).
Empty cup scoops 1 sip; vanilla glass bottle or matching empty bottle scoops up to 4 sips. Mixing drinks is blocked safely.
Protect yourself from hot oil splashes and Level 3 Extreme Spicy lip-flames with a cloth apron:
Equip: wears in the chestplate slot with real leather-tier protection (3 armor, 80 durability), taking normal wear and enchantments.
Craft: in 3×3, 1 string at top-center + 6 white wool across the middle and bottom rows.
Repair: repair on an anvil using white wool or string.
◆ Three styles and recoloring
All three styles share identical armor, durability, enchantability, and repair materials — only the pattern changes:
Style　Look
Plain off-white linen (default)
Indigo dyed cloth with tiny white floral print
Off-white apron with dark brown trim and a hem pocket
Recoloring: combine any apron style + dye shapelessly —
Any style + white dye → linen
Any style + blue dye → blue print
Any style + brown dye → brown trim
Recoloring updates the same apron while keeping durability, enchantments, and custom names; matching dye returns it untouched.
Tip
b: How it looks worn: hugs the front torso down to just above the knees, swinging naturally with your steps and resting flat across your lap when seated, with transparent sleeves/back and just the neck strap behind.

blocks.t: While worn:
No lip flames on Extreme Spice: eating Level 3 Extreme Spicy food or broth no longer lights the 2-second mouth flame (purely visual when unarmored, never deals damage).

Splash shield within 4 blocks: standing within 4 blocks of a lit stove, lit campfire, fire block, or lava grants immunity to close-range burn/lava/hot-floor splash ticks and extinguishes flames on you (direct lava wading, mobs, and falls still hurt normally).
Tip
b: Stay close to the heat: splash protection requires an active heat source within 4 blocks; step away and it behaves like ordinary armor.

blocks.t: Open hotpot screen: hold chopsticks and Shift + right-click pot.
Pick up cooked food from pot: plain right-click pot to grab a cooked item from that cell.
Pick up from bowls/plates: right-click to lift the last-added item.
Add raw food to pot: right-click pot while holding raw food on chopsticks.
Eat: hold right-click with cooked food on chopsticks (works even when full, adding saturation and sauce buffs).
Return to plate/bowl: sneak + right-click center while holding food.
Dip: right-click a placed sauce bowl while holding food; see Dipping Sauces.

Rest on bowl or plate rims: Shift + right-click the rim to perch chopsticks inward from that side (carrying held food along); clicking the center empty-handed rests on your facing side, snapped to 22.5° steps (empty-hand right-click picks back up; breaking drops both).

Rest flat on tabletops: aim at an empty spot on any low/tall hotpot table and Shift + right-click to place chopsticks intact with a porcelain mini chopstick rest — two parallel 8.5 px bamboo sticks resting tips across the saddle and ends facing you across all 4 cardinal directions (occupying 9.5×4.5 px near the clicked spot; empty-hand right-click or mining retrieves chopsticks + held food cleanly without dropping a separate rest).
Tip
b: Rim resting vs tabletop resting are separate placements: bowls/plates hold chopsticks on their rims, while empty tabletops add the porcelain rest. Pick up empty-handed before moving.

blocks.t: Tip
b: Eat even when full: every mod food item can be eaten on a full hunger bar, topping up saturation up to 20; compatible with Always Eat.

blocks.t: Hotpot belongs around a table. The mod provides low hotpot tables (Hotpot Table, ground height) and tall hotpot tables (Tall Hotpot Table, 1.5 blocks tall), three prep racks (floor, desktop, and hanging), plus two styles of wooden seats across 11 woods:

40 legacy tables consolidated into 2 universal tables: the earlier 11 wood low tables, 11 wood tall tables, and 18 stone/metal tables have been unified into Hotpot Table and Tall Hotpot Table, crafted with any vanilla planks (#minecraft:planks) and styled freely by swapping materials.
All hotpot tables are uniformly non-flammable: even wooden-styled tables never catch fire from nearby heat.

Tabletop sits flush with a short stove's bricks, letting the stove nest seamlessly inside a table ring.
Stepped underside recesses 4 pixels along outer edges for knee room.
Auto-connects: joins adjacent tables (low or tall) and stoves automatically, and seals inner brick legs and tabletop edges cleanly on 3×3 rings or inside corners with zero hollow gaps.
Uniformly non-flammable with hardness 2.0 (breakable empty-handed), while mining speed, break particles, and step/hit sounds dynamically match the applied part material.
1.5 blocks tall, with an overhanging top and 4-pixel recessed legs for legroom.
Built on a lower brick section topped with planks (crafted from 3 vanilla bricks + 3 any planks).
Pairs with a tall stove: facing a stove's firebox automatically removes bricks on that side so flames stay visible.
Connects seamlessly to adjacent low tables, tall tables, and stoves, and stays non-flammable (hardness 2.0, empty-hand breakable).
Taller hitbox lets you directly target tableware resting on top without misclicking behind the table.
◆ Placing items on tables
Plates, bowls, drinks, and sauce bowls sit neatly on tabletops — see Tableware & Drinks.
Small decorations (lanterns, flower pots, candles, cakes, and table_decorations blocks such as Desktop Prep Rack) snap flush to the tabletop instead of floating.
Other full blocks float 5 pixels above low tables or embed 7 pixels into tall tables for decorative variety.
Once you craft a universal Hotpot Table or Tall Hotpot Table, customize its tabletop and base independently on the spot (works with opaque solid blocks from other mods too):
Per-part replacement (1-in-1-out refund): hold any eligible solid block (full opaque cube, non-emissive, no block entity, not blacklisted) and right-click without sneaking:
Aim at the upper section (top surface & apron rim) to replace the tabletop material;
Aim at the lower section (legs / base) to replace the base material (on tall tables, swaps both middle band and bottom brick base together);
Consumes 1 held block; if that part already carried a custom material, the previous block is returned 1-for-1 losslessly (default built-in oak planks / bricks do not drop extra blocks).
Sneak controls:
Sneak + empty-hand right-click a part: ejects its custom material block back to you and restores the default look;
Sneak + block right-click: bypasses material swapping so you can build against the table normally.

Mining feedback & retention: mining speed, break particles, and sounds match the targeted part's material — mining the top spills tabletop particles while mining the base spills base particles — while retaining hardness 2.0 (breakable empty-handed); breaking or middle-clicking preserves swapped appearances.

Migrated legacy tables: appearances migrated from the 40 older preset tables remain intact, but cannot be popped out with sneak + empty hand (to prevent item duplication); hold any new solid block and right-click directly to override.
Material scope config: adjust table_materials.mode in Config ("Tables & Rack Materials") or JSON:
any_solid (default): any full opaque non-container block matching allow/deny tags (table_materials_allow / table_materials_deny);
tag_only: restrict strictly to the allowlist tag;
off: disable material swapping.

The 9 stone and metal styles introduced in 0.1.4-alpha (smooth stone, polished andesite / diorite / granite / deepslate / blackstone, quartz, cut copper, and iron — formerly 18 separate tables) are now unified into the per-part material swapping system in 0.3.1-alpha: craft Hotpot Table or Tall Hotpot Table and right-click the tabletop with the desired stone or metal block. Legacy stone/metal tables already placed or stored in old saves upgrade automatically with their looks intact.

Prep racks store plates, ingredients, cloth aprons, and handy utensils with GUI-less slot-targeted direct placement and retrieval (right-click a slot to place, spilling to the next free slot if occupied; empty-hand right-click removes; breaking drops all contents). When enabled, all racks also support whole-rack material swapping via solid blocks (sneak + empty hand pops the block back; controlled by mode.rack_swap_materials and table_materials.mode):

Multi-Tier Prep Rack (6-slot floor rack): 3-tier iron-and-wood floor frame with 2 slots per shelf (6 slots total), holding plates/bowls (#rack_plates and tabletop items) plus cookable or edible ingredients.

Desktop Prep Rack (4-slot desktop rack): two-step tabletop organizer (2 lower front slots + 2 upper rear slots, 4 slots total). Tagged under table_decorations, so placing it on low or tall hotpot tables automatically aligns it flush with the tabletop.

Hanging Prep Rack (4-slot wall / ceiling rack): 4 hanging hooks that auto-select wall (against block sides) or ceiling (under ceilings) upon placement. Designed for #rack_hangables tools (iron kitchen knife, rolling pin, bamboo chopsticks, wooden press lid, shears, buckets) plus all 3 cloth aprons (Linen Cloth Apron, Blue Print Cloth Apron, Brown Trim Cloth Apron).
Simple Mode
b: Prep-rack material swapping is disabled in this mode; storing and taking plates, utensils, and aprons still works normally.

◆ Placement
Facing: placed facing the same direction as the player.

Bench rows: two aligned seats of the same height auto-join into a long bench (removing inner legs and inset outer legs; perpendicular seats stay separate), up to 3 blocks long, regardless of placement direction.
Benches feature tilted "A"-frame legs with a clean full-width hitbox so walking beside them never snags.
◆ Stacking benches into ladders
Each bench is 1 block tall, so stacked benches double as climbable stairs.
Right-click an existing bench while holding another bench (no sneaking) to automatically stack onto the very top of that column, consuming 1 bench.
Aiming directly at the top face does the same.
Stacks up to 16 layers high.
Stacks of 2 or more layers turn into a climbable ladder from any side by walking forward or jumping (single benches never climb accidentally).
Top bench remains sittable with an empty hand; covered middle benches cannot be sat on.
Stacking onto an occupied bench gently dismounts the seated player first.
Mining removes one bench at a time and drops anyone sitting on it safely.
Tip
b: Stack and break freely: build high shelves or cozy "upper bunks" beside the pot. Stacking benches onto benches or climbing a bench tower unlocks the "Climbing Higher" advancement.

blocks.t: ◆ Sitting
Right-click a seat with an empty hand (or any non-block item) to sit down.
Click the center to sit centered, or click the seam between two joined seats to sit astride the joint.
Players leave at least one full block of spacing so they never clip together.
Press Shift (sneak) to dismount behind the bench.
Tip
b: Recommended pairings: benches + tall tables + tall stoves, and stools + low tables + short stoves so heights align cleanly.
